headline: intg-prod-a1: setroubleshootd at 99.7% CPU and recurring nightly memory exhaustion — cause not established, audit log outstanding, convergence blocked
known: Process snapshot at 2026-03-17T19:00:00+00:00 shows pid 3501048 (setroubleshootd, user audit-analysis) at 99.7% CPU with 79h 58m cumulative CPU time, started 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00.
SELinux is confirmed in enforcing mode; denials are real and being logged.
Integration service JVM (pid 3489339) is at 5.6% CPU with a resident set of 24.8 GiB at snapshot time.
Memory exhaustion problems P-4100 through P-4112 all opened in the early-morning window 03:00–04:00 UTC and auto-closed approximately 2.5 hours later, repeating nightly from 2026-03-02 onward.
Memory series shows a rising sawtooth pattern beginning 2026-03-02T00:00:00+00:00.
All 13 problems in the window are unacknowledged; the observability platform notes no problem in this window was acknowledged, assigned, or actioned.
CHG-88104 records installation of endpoint-compliance-agent 7.4.2-27 on 2026-02-22.
The audit-analysis-server package has been installed for 3 years; the 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 start of setroubleshootd is an activation event, not an installation event.
No heap or thread dump has been collected from the JVM.
User-reported symptoms are batch transfer latency and console slowness on intg-prod-a1.

suspected.statement: setroubleshootd is consuming approximately 100% CPU in response to a high-volume stream of SELinux AVC denials that began on 2026-03-02, and this CPU saturation correlates with batch transfer latency and console slowness on intg-prod-a1. Confidence: supported. No direct observation of AVC denial volume or rate exists; the audit log is outstanding, so the link between setroubleshootd CPU consumption and a denial storm remains inferential.
suspected.falsifying_test: Inspect /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC denial counts per hour from 2026-03-02 onward; if denial volume is low or absent, setroubleshootd CPU consumption has a different cause not yet identified.

suspected.statement: The installation of endpoint-compliance-agent 7.4.2-27 (CHG-88104) on 2026-02-22 triggered novel SELinux AVC denials that activated setroubleshootd on 2026-03-02, initiating the CPU and memory exhaustion pattern. Confidence: plausible. CHG-88104 is the only change record in the pre-onset window per the change correlator (confidence: plausible), but an 8-day gap separates installation from onset, weakening temporal proximity. The registry carries a confirmed caveat — self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true — meaning the version running at onset may differ from 7.4.2-27 with no registry evidence. No AVC denial log has been collected to confirm the agent is the source domain of the denials.
suspected.falsifying_test: Inspect /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC denials from 2026-02-22 through 2026-03-02; if no denials are attributable to the endpoint-compliance-agent source domain, this hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, confirm whether the agent was active and consuming memory between 2026-02-22 and 2026-03-01; flat memory during that period weakens the correlation.

suspected.statement: The integration service JVM has a memory leak contributing to the rising sawtooth memory pattern, with the JVM's resident set growing during each batch cycle and partially recovering, compounding the memory exhaustion alongside setroubleshootd. Confidence: plausible. The current resident set of 24.8 GiB is elevated above the 23.1 GiB steady-state standing condition but not dramatically so. The sharp sawtooth reset is more consistent with a process restart or GC event than a leak, which would typically not recover without intervention. JVM CPU at 5.6% is inconsistent with a runaway workload driving memory growth.
suspected.falsifying_test: Collect a JVM heap dump from pid 3489339; if heap occupancy is stable and within historical norms, the JVM is not contributing to the memory growth pattern. Swap metrics would also clarify whether the JVM is being paged out during exhaustion events.
suspected.precedent: Prior incident INC-2411 describes memory exhaustion on an integration-class host with a JVM workload. Divergence from that incident: INC-2411 had a recorded heap configuration change, which is absent here.

suspected.statement: The recurring nightly memory exhaustion events (P-4100 through P-4112) have been auto-closing without acknowledgement for 15 days, masking a progressive degradation that has now manifested as user-visible latency. Confidence: supported. Auto-close could reflect genuine recovery if the batch workload completes and memory is released; the pattern alone does not confirm suppression of a worsening condition.
suspected.falsifying_test: Compare batch transfer completion times and console response times on days when problems were open versus closed; if performance is identical in both states, the auto-closing events are not causing user-visible impact.
suspected.precedent: Prior incident INC-2419 describes the same pattern: same signature, same auto-close behaviour, ran 10 days unacknowledged before action. Divergence from that incident: INC-2419 was resolved by restart without establishing cause — that outcome must not be repeated here.

outstanding: Audit denial log for the affected window, showing source domain and denied action per denial — requested from platform_team 149 minutes ago, still not received. This is the deciding evidence for the primary causal chain.

Currently running version of endpoint-compliance-agent on intg-prod-a1, to determine whether it has self-updated beyond 7.4.2-27 since 2026-02-22 — requested from security_engineering, still outstanding.

setroubleshootd log (/var/log/setroubleshoot/setroubleshoot.log) from 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 onward, to identify which SELinux denials are being analysed and whether volume is consistent with 99.7% CPU — requested from security_engineering, still outstanding.

JVM heap and thread dump from pid 3489339 (integration-service) to characterise whether memory growth is attributable to a workload change or internal behaviour since 2026-03-02 — requested from platform_engineering, still outstanding.

Swap utilisation metric series for intg-prod-a1 at 1h resolution from 2026-03-02 to present, to determine whether the JVM or other processes are being paged out during exhaustion events — requested from platform_engineering, still outstanding.
standing_conditions: The integration service JVM on intg-prod-a1 holds 23.1 GiB resident of 32 GiB total RAM as steady state for at least 6 months, with no alerting configured and no owner assigned. This leaves only approximately 8.9 GiB free at baseline, meaning any additional persistent process materially reduces the margin before memory exhaustion. This condition did not cause the incident but explains why a new consumer was able to trigger exhaustion.

13 memory exhaustion problems (P-4100 through P-4112) fired and auto-closed over 15 days with zero acknowledgements, zero assignments, and zero actions taken. The auto-close behaviour created a false impression of self-resolution and allowed a progressive degradation to reach user-visible impact undetected. Alerting configuration and on-call response procedures for auto-closing problems on this host require review as a post-incident finding.

The non-production equivalent host (intg-nonprod-a1) has build_parity=false with a different patch level and different installed agents. The non-prod environment cannot be used to safely reproduce or test hypotheses about production behaviour without accounting for these differences.

The change registry has a confirmed blind spot: self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true. Agents that self-update do not produce package records, meaning the current running version of any self-updating agent on this host may differ from the registry without any audit trail. This is a standing gap in change visibility for this host.
No pipeline deployments are recorded for intg-prod-a1; any application-layer change delivered outside the pipeline is invisible to the change registry. This is a standing gap in change traceability.

incident_commander: do not restart setroubleshootd or the integration service JVM until the audit log and setroubleshootd log have been collected and the source of AVC denials identified. A restart would suppress the symptom without establishing the cause and would destroy in-memory state needed for diagnosis. Authorisation is required before any such action.

incident_commander: notify business stakeholders that the investigation is active, that batch latency correlates with host resource exhaustion under investigation, and that no transfers have failed; provide next update time.
